4B.01.t: Volar Approach to the Distal Radius — FCR (Modified Henry)
4B.01.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Volar FCR approach |
|---|---|
| Uses | Most distal radius fractures, malunion osteotomy, volar Barton (Campbell; AO) |
| Position | Supine, arm board, **forearm supinated**; tourniquet without full exsanguination → veins show the artery (Hopp) |
| Incision | 8 cm on the **radial border of FCR** (flexor carpi radialis); diagonal limb across the crease → more room (Campbell; AO) |
| Plane | Distal Henry = **BR (radial) / FCR (median)**; modified = **FCR sheath**, ulnar to the radial artery (Hopp; AO) |
| Superficial | Open the FCR sheath and floor → FCR retracted, **FPL** (flexor pollicis longus) swept ulnar by finger (AO; Campbell) |
| Deep | **L-shaped PQ** (pronator quadratus) cut: horizontal at the **watershed line**, vertical on the radial border → lift with periosteum (AO) |

[[FIG: Fig 4B.2 · 4B.01

- Joint line → find with a needle; PQ cut stays a few mm proximal (AO)
- Styloid won't reduce → release **BR** (brachioradialis) from it; not reattached (AO; Campbell)

### Dangers and the plate
| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **Radial artery** | Radial side of the interval | Stay in the sheath; venae comitantes mark it (Hopp) |
| **Palmar cutaneous branch** of median | Ulnar, near the FCR sheath | Don't stray ulnar to FCR or catch it in closure (AO) |
| **FPL** | Rubs on a plate past the watershed line | Plate **at or proximal** to the line (Campbell) |
| Extensor tendons | Dorsal screw tips | Screws **2 mm shorter** than measured; skyline view (Campbell) |
| SRN | Under BR if you go radial | Warn of transient tingling (Hopp) |

[[FIG: Fig 4B.3 · 4B.01

- Plate → K-wire from the styloid → 3 shaft screws → distal screws ulnar to radial, 2 per fragment (Operative sheet)
- Joint screws → check on a lateral **tilted 20–25°** (Operative sheet)
- Proximal extension → full Henry (→ 3B); PIN (posterior interosseous nerve) only in the proximal third (Hopp)
- Close → PQ over the plate (AO); Campbell → optional, no effect on outcome

CLINICAL PEARL — bridge plate and the ulnar styloid
- Dorsal bridge plate (Burke–Singer) → two 4 cm incisions: index MC (metacarpal) + dorsoradial radius (Campbell)
  - Plate slid **under the 2nd compartment**, radius → 2nd MC (Campbell)
- Ulnar styloid → fix only if **displaced + DRUJ (distal radioulnar joint) unstable** after radius fixation (Campbell)

PITFALL — which way does FCR go?
- AO and Campbell's scaphoid approach → FCR retracted **ulnarly**
- Campbell's volar plate technique → FCR retracted **radially** (protects the median nerve)
- Say → "either is fine; the **radial artery stays radial, the median nerve ulnar**"

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "volar approach to the distal radius"
- Supine, supinated → incision on the **radial border of FCR**
- FCR sheath → FPL swept ulnar → **L-shaped PQ** release
- Plate **proximal to the watershed line** → else FPL rupture
- At risk → radial artery (radial), palmar cutaneous branch (ulnar), FPL, extensors (long screws)
- Extend → proximally into Henry (BR/FCR plane)

4B.02.t: Dorsal Approach to the Wrist — 3rd/4th Compartment
4B.02.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Dorsal wrist |
|---|---|
| Uses | Dorsal shear/impaction fractures, perilunate dislocation, wrist fusion, PRC (proximal row carpectomy), rheumatoid synovectomy (Hopp; Campbell) |
| Position | Supine, **forearm pronated** on an arm board, tourniquet (Hopp) |
| Incision | 8 cm straight over Lister's tubercle, midway between the styloids, 3 cm above → 5 cm below the joint (Hopp) |
| Plane | **None** → all muscles PIN-supplied → go between compartments (Hopp; Netter) |
| Superficial | Straight to the retinaculum → **full-thickness** flaps carry the cutaneous nerves (Hopp) |
| Deep | Open the **3rd** along EPL (extensor pollicis longus) → EPL on a loop → lift the **4th** subperiosteally, intact → capsule (AO) |

[[FIG: Fig 4B.4 · 4B.02

- Radial column → add a 1st/2nd compartment window, SRN above it (AO)
- Arthrotomy → leave **1 mm of capsule** on the radius for repair (AO)
- Retinaculum → attaches to pisiform and triquetrum, not ulna → keep a distal strip so EPL glides (Hopp; AO)

### Capsule, dangers and closure
| Item | Say |
|---|---|
| Capsule | **Radially based ligament-sparing flap** along DRC (dorsal radiocarpal) and DIC (dorsal intercarpal) fibres (Berger–Bishop) (Campbell; AO) |
| At risk | **EPL** (rupture on plate or Lister's), SRN and dorsal ulnar branch (neuroma), radial artery laterally (Hopp) |
| PIN | Terminal branch on the **floor of the 4th** → excise for pain (PIN neurectomy) (Campbell) |
| Close | 2nd and 4th under EPL; retinacular flap between plate and EPL, or EPL left subcutaneous (AO) |
| Extension | No plane → not up the whole radius; distally to the metacarpals (Hopp) |
| Perilunate | Dorsal first → SL (scapholunate) K-wires or screw + anchors, LT (lunotriquetral) K-wires; add volar **extended CTR** (ulnar to palmaris longus) for CTS (≈25%) and LT; >6 weeks → no closed reduction (Hand sheet; Operative sheet) |

[[FIG: Fig 4B.5 · 4B.02

- Say → "**ligament-sparing flap**; a longitudinal cut divides the DIC"

4B.03.t: Dorsoulnar Approach — DRUJ, TFCC & Distal Ulna
4B.03.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Dorsoulnar (5th/6th compartment) |
|---|---|
| Uses | Foveal TFCC (triangular fibrocartilage complex) repair, DRUJ reconstruction, ulnar head and styloid surgery (Campbell) |
| Incision | Hockey stick 5–6 cm between **5th (EDM, extensor digiti minimi) and 6th (ECU, extensor carpi ulnaris)** over the ulnar head; turn radially distal to the ulnar pole (Campbell) |
| Plane | None → compartment interval |
| Deep | Floor of the 5th → transverse capsulotomy proximal to the TFCC + inverted T distal to it (Campbell) |
| Volar window | 3 cm between ulnar bundle and flexors → palmar DRUJ (Campbell) |

[[FIG: Fig 4B.6 · 4B.03

- Distal ulna shaft → straight incision between **ECU and FCU** (flexor carpi ulnaris) (AO; Campbell)
- Radial-sided tear (1D) → 4th/5th interval instead (Campbell)
- Irreducible DRUJ → ECU often the block → same route (Hand sheet; Trauma sheet)

| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **Dorsal ulnar cutaneous branch** | Leaves ≈5 cm above the wrist, winds dorsal round the ulnar head | Angle radially; find it before deepening (Campbell; AO) |
| ECU subsheath | Floor of the 6th | Don't open → ECU subluxes |
| TFCC | Under the capsule | Proximal capsulotomy first (Campbell) |

[[FIG: Fig 4B.7 · 4B.03

### DRUJ and TFCC — what to do through it
| Problem | Do |
|---|---|
| TFCC 1A (central) | Debride, up to **80%** of the disc |
| TFCC 1B–1D | Repair |
| Type 2 + ulnar plus or arthritis | Distal ulna resection (Darrach or Sauvé–Kapandji) |
| DRUJ with a radius fracture | Fix the radius → test; stable → splint 4–6 wk |
| Still unstable | Fragment → fix styloid base or sigmoid notch; none → **K-wire 4–6 wk** (dorsal dislocation pinned in supination) |
| Chronic instability | Correct malunion first → **Adams–Berger** graft (best), Herbert capsulorrhaphy, Fulkerson–Watson tenodesis |
| Arthritic DRUJ | **Darrach** → elderly, low demand · **Sauvé–Kapandji** → young, high demand · Weaver hemiresection |

- Hand sheet; Trauma sheet

4B.04.t: Volar Approach to the Wrist — Carpal Tunnel Release
4B.04.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Open carpal tunnel release |
|---|---|
| Uses | CTS (carpal tunnel syndrome), flexor synovectomy, lunate dislocation, midpalmar sepsis (Hopp) |
| Position | Supine, forearm supinated on a hand table, tourniquet (Hopp) |
| Incision | **Mini-palm** → 2–3 cm in line with the **radial border of the ring finger**, distal wrist crease → Kaplan's line (Campbell) |
| Plane | None → anatomic dissection (Hopp) |
| Superficial | Palmar fascia → TCL (transverse carpal ligament) |
| Deep | Dissector between TCL and nerve → cut on the **ulnar side** of the nerve, 2–3 mm left on the hamate hook (Hopp; Campbell) |

[[FIG: Fig 4B.8 · 4B.04

- Proximal end → divide the distal 2 cm of antebrachial fascia **under vision**, never blind (Campbell)
- Extend → proximally between PL (palmaris longus) and FCR; distally into a finger zigzag (Hopp)
- Rheumatoid synovectomy → feel the floor: FPL rupture over a **scaphoid spur** = Mannerfelt syndrome (Nagah p19)

### Dangers
| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **Motor branch** | Radial side; through the TCL in ≈20% | See it before cutting (Hopp) |
| **Palmar cutaneous branch** | Ulnar to FCR, over the TCL | Ring finger axis (Campbell) |
| **Superficial palmar arch** | 5–8 mm distal to the TCL edge | Stop at the **deep palmar fat** (= complete release); distal end **under vision** (Campbell) |
| Ulnar nerve/artery | Ulnar to the hook | Stay radial to the hook |

[[FIG: Fig 4B.9 · 4B.04

- Endoscopic (Agee) → portal at the proximal crease; blade in the ring finger line, hugging the hook; "**when in doubt, get out**" (Campbell)
- Endoscopic → same outcome, slightly more nerve injury, ≈1% conversion; not in revision or with a mass (Campbell)
- Failure → incomplete release, re-formed TCL, scar, neuroma, wrong diagnosis or level, double crush (Campbell; Nagah p37)

CLINICAL PEARL — endoscopic safe zone and recurrent CTS
- Blade safe zone → triangle: median nerve ulnar border, long–ring common digital nerve, superficial arch (Campbell)
- Recurrent CTS → neurolysis + **hypothenar fat pad flap** → best secondary results (Campbell)

PITFALL — where to cut the skin?
- Hoppenfeld → curved, just ulnar and parallel to the thenar crease
- Campbell → that line "not advisable" → palmar cutaneous branch at risk → **ring finger axis**
- Say → "**in line with the radial border of the ring finger**, ulnar to the thenar crease"

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "carpal tunnel release — safe steps"
- Incision → ring finger axis, distal crease to Kaplan's line
- TCL cut on the **ulnar side** of the nerve → motor branch is radial
- Distal limit → palmar fat → superficial arch beyond
- Strip left on the hamate hook → flexors don't sublux ulnar
- Check the motor branch: extra-, sub- or transligamentous

|---|---|

4B.06.b:
### Volar and dorsal — side by side
| | Volar (Russe / FCR) | Dorsal |
|---|---|---|
| Uses | **Waist and distal pole**, humpback correction, graft (AO; Campbell) | **Proximal pole**, SL ligament, with a distal radius fracture (AO) |
| Position | Supinated, wrist extended over a towel | Pronated, **wrist flexed** for the pole |
| Incision | Over distal FCR to the tubercle, then 2 cm distal-radial to the STT (scaphotrapeziotrapezoid) joint (AO; Operative sheet) | Straight from Lister's tubercle ≈3 cm distal (AO) |
| Interval | FCR sheath; FCR ulnar, radial artery radial (Hopp; Campbell) | 3rd compartment → EPL radial, 4th ulnar (AO) |
| Capsule | Oblique; **RSC (± LRL) divided → repair** (AO; Campbell) | Longitudinal/T, radius → DIC (AO) |
| At risk | **Superficial palmar branch** of the radial artery → retract or ligate; RSC | **Dorsal ridge vessels**; SRN |
| Wire | Volar edge of the distal pole, aimed 30–45° dorsal and 30–45° ulnar (Operative sheet) | Proximal pole, down the central axis |
| Screw | Headless, countersunk, **4–5 mm shorter** than measured (Hand sheet) | Same |

[[FIG: Fig 4B.11 · 4B.06

- RSC = radioscaphocapitate, LRL = long radiolunate → unrepaired → carpal instability, palmar tilt (AO)
- Dorsal → don't strip the **dorsal ridge** → the proximal pole lives on it (→ 4A 4.03)
- Percutaneous → ≈1 cm stab distal to the STT for a waist <2 mm displaced (AO)
  - Dorsal (Slade) → flex and pronate until the poles line up ("ring") (Campbell)

| Nonunion (Geissler) | Do |
|---|---|
| No cyst | Screw alone, percutaneous |
| Cyst 1–5 mm | Inlay graft → **Matti** dorsal, **Russe** volar |
| Large cyst or humpback | Volar **wedge** graft |
| AVN (avascular necrosis) or failed graft | Vascularised → **1,2-ICSRA** (intercompartmental supraretinacular artery) or free MFC (medial femoral condyle) |

- Hand sheet

### Dorsolateral (Hoppenfeld)
- Gently curved over the **snuffbox**, 1st MC base → 3 cm above; plane **EPL / EPB** (extensor pollicis brevis; both PIN, proximal) (Hopp)

### Total wrist fusion
- Indications → post-traumatic arthritis (SLAC, scapholunate advanced collapse; SNAC, scaphoid nonunion advanced collapse), RA (rheumatoid arthritis), failed salvage, spasticity (Campbell)
  [[FIG: Fig 4B.27 · 4B.13

### Tendon transfers
| Function | Transfer |
|---|---|
| Wrist extension | PT (pronator teres) → **ECRB** (extensor carpi radialis brevis) → central; into ECRL → radial deviation (Nagah p38) |
| Finger extension | FCR or FCU → EDC (Hand sheet) |
| Thumb extension | PL → EPL (Hand sheet) |
| Opposition | FDS ring → APB (abductor pollicis brevis) via an FCU pulley (Hand sheet) |
| Thumb flexion | BR → FPL (Hand sheet) |
| Claw | ECRL → lumbricals, or FDS lasso round A1 (Hand sheet) |
